ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows an ideal operational amplifier inverting circuit, with the non-inverting terminal “+” grounded; the input voltage ui is connected to the inverting input node through resistor R1; the feedback branch from the output terminal u0 back to the inverting input node is composed of resistor R2 and capacitor C connected in series. Reasoning: Under linear negative feedback in an ideal op-amp, the inverting terminal is a virtual ground, and the input-end current flows through R1 into the feedback impedance. Using the complex impedance method, in the s domain the capacitor impedance is ZC=1/(Cs), therefore the feedback impedance is Zf=R2+1/(Cs)=(R2Cs+1)/(Cs). The transfer function of the inverting amplifier is U0(s)/Ui(s)=-Zf/R1, so G(s)=U0(s)/Ui(s)=-[(R2Cs+1)/(Cs)]/R1=-(R2Cs+1)/(R1Cs).

raw_record.question_text: Given the active electrical network as shown in the image, use the complex impedance method to find the transfer function \( \frac{U_0(s)}{U_i(s)} \).

method.method_draft: Identify the circuit as an ideal inverting op-amp with input impedance R1 and feedback impedance equal to the series combination of R2 and C. In the s-domain, replace the capacitor by 1/(Cs), so Zf = R2 + 1/(Cs) = (R2 C s + 1)/(C s). Apply the inverting amplifier formula G(s)=U0(s)/Ui(s)=-Zf/R1 to obtain G(s)=-(R2 C s + 1)/(R1 C s).

method.method_draft: Let the inverting input node voltage be v. Because the + input is grounded and the op-amp is ideal with feedback, set v=0. The input branch current term is (v-Ui)/R1, and the feedback branch impedance is Zf=R2+1/(Cs), giving feedback current term (v-U0)/Zf. Apply KCL at the node: (v-Ui)/R1 + (v-U0)/Zf = 0. Substitute v=0 and solve: -Ui/R1 - U0/Zf = 0, so U0/Ui = -Zf/R1 = -(R2 + 1/(Cs))/R1 = -(R2 C s + 1)/(R1 C s).
